items.summary: World action models (WAMs) predict actions and future observations, typically from a reconstruction-based representation that carries noisy, redundant information which can complicate downstream predictions. We introduce LeWAM, a bidirectional transformer for forward, backward, inverse dynamics and policy prediction, on a decoder-free JEPA latent trained end-to-end through all four modes. We see the following benefits: 1) Alignment: linear probes read robot and object state from LeWAM's latent better than from a regular Le World Model (a forward-only JEPA world model), while the latent ignores visual distractors as well as LeWM does and far better than a reconstruction-based WAM. 2) Acting: Closed-loop evaluations of LeWAM match a regular flow-matching policy trained on the same encoder at matched size, while also providing a world model. 3) Planning: Sampling raw actions when planning with WAMs lets MPC exploit dynamics-model inaccuracies; planning in the noise space of the policy head instead improves the closed-loop performance of these WAMs.
items.title: LeWAM: A JEPA World Action Model with Diffusion-Steering-Based MPC

items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping how information is produced, accessed, and circulated, while enabling disinformation campaigns of increasing scale and sophistication. There is currently no clear evidence that fully autonomous AI swarms conduct influence operations at scale, but their enabling capabilities are advancing. We define malicious AI swarms as coordinated, persistent, and adaptive multi-agent systems designed for influence operations, distinguishing them from AI-assisted content production and centrally managed synthetic personas. We examine their implications for hybrid regimes and conflict-affected states in Africa, where institutional constraints and fragile media environments may heighten vulnerability. Drawing on Mali and Ethiopia, we consider how automated influence could infiltrate communities, fabricate consensus, and erode trust in governance and development. The cases illustrate different configurations of state and non-state influence: competing actors in Mali's fragmented information environment, and more organized state-led strategies of narrative management in Ethiopia. African-language and training-data asymmetries may constrain influence capabilities while weakening defensive responses. Hybrid human-AI operations could combine automated scale and adaptation with local knowledge and credibility. This forward-looking risk analysis develops a scenario of increasingly accessible AI-driven coordination, rather than claiming that autonomous swarms are already operating at scale in Africa. We propose a layered governance approach linking technical safeguards to platform accountability, civic institutions, and regional coordination to protect democratic participation, peacebuilding, and development.
items.title: Automated Disinformation and Malicious AI Swarms: Risks for Democracy and Development in Africa

items.summary: This paper develops a new predefined-time integral reinforcement learning framework for optimal control of unknown nonlinear systems. The unknown drift is first approximated by a radial basis function (RBF) neural network, together with a data-driven online identification law for updating the corresponding neural weights. After the identifier converges to a sufficiently small neighborhood of the true dynamics, the learned model is incorporated into the integral reinforcement learning (IRL) problem. Unlike conventional reinforcement-learning-based optimal control, the desired convergence time is introduced directly into the control objective: a Lyapunov function and its prescribed decay behavior are specified by the designer, and inverse-optimal control is then used to construct a compatible running cost whose optimal policy inherits the predefined-time stabilization property. The value function is approximated by a second RBF neural network, and a new critic update law is developed to impose predefined-time convergence on the critic weights. Finite informative learning data are stored in a replay buffer and reused during the critic update, thereby avoiding the need for persistent excitation throughout the closed-loop operation. Theoretical analysis proves that the critic-weight error enters a prescribed residual set within the allocated learning horizon, while the closed-loop state reaches a small neighborhood of the origin within the overall designer-specified deadline. Numerical simulations on an unknown nonlinear system verify accurate drift reconstruction, predefined-time critic learning, and closed-loop convergence.
items.title: Predefined-Time Integral Reinforcement Learning for Unknown Nonlinear Systems via Inverse-Optimal Design

items.summary: We study the relation between equal-weight circle quadrature, Gauss--Chebyshev quadrature, and planar Minkowski reconstruction. The regular $N$-point grid is an $\mathbb S^1$-design of strength $N-1$; a half-step rotation of the $2M$-point grid projects to the classical $M$-point Gauss--Chebyshev rule. A common family of quadrature-error functionals gives exact identities for integration error, mixed-area error, and support-function error. For $N\ge3$, the centered Minkowski polygon $P_N$ with perimeter $2π$ has the exact Hausdorff distance from the unit disk $B^2$ \[ d_H(P_N,B^2)=1-\fracπ{N}\cot\fracπ{N} =\frac{π^2}{3N^2}+O(N^{-4}). \] With Steiner centering, we obtain $d_H(K_μ,K_ν)\leπW_1(μ,ν)$ for balanced, nondegenerate probability measures, where $W_1$ uses geodesic distance. Its exponent is sharp even for smooth positive densities near the uniform measure. The identity $W_1(ν_N,σ)=π/(2N)$ yields a general $O(N^{-1})$ bound for the regular grid. The sharper $O(N^{-2})$ rate follows from the sparse discrepancy spectrum and the inverse multiplier $(1-k^2)^{-1}$. Finally, a perturbation estimate gives sufficient conditions for preserving the quadratic rate and its leading constant.
items.title: Gauss--Chebyshev Quadrature, $\mathbb S^1$-Designs, and the Planar Minkowski Inverse Problem: A One-Dimensional Model for Design-Induced Convex Geometry

items.summary: An inventory of marketing instruments identifies what higher education institutions use; the present article examines the stages each instrument can reach, its cost, and the distribution of promotional expenditure across the instrument portfolio. The analysis covers twelve marketing instruments accounting for UZS 5,618 million in sector-wide promotional expenditure. Three constructs organise the analysis. Portfolio concentration compares the distribution of promotional expenditure with the distribution of observed outcomes. Conversion efficiency is examined through cost per application and stage reach, the latter introduced here as the furthest stage of the applicant decision process at which an instrument can directly engage the prospective student, ranging from awareness to the commitment decision. Absorptive capacity, also introduced here, represents the amount of additional budget that a relatively efficient instrument can absorb before its cost advantage is exhausted under the specified scaling assumptions. The results reveal a marked inverse relationship between current budget allocation and measured cost efficiency. Cost per application is strongly negatively correlated with stage reach (r = −0.905), while budget share is positively correlated with cost per application (r = 0.654). Instruments limited to the awareness stage account for 48.8 per cent of the budget and generate 25.3 per cent of applications, at a mean cost of UZS 112 thousand per application. By contrast, instruments capable of reaching the commitment decision account for 10.6 per cent of the budget and generate 24.5 per cent of applications, at a mean cost of UZS 20.8 thousand per application. The corresponding cost ratio is 5.40, with a Welch statistic of 8.14. The four instruments capable of carrying claims that prospective students can independently verify are also the four instruments that reach the commitment stage, yet together they account for approximately one-tenth of the promotional budget. The apparent scope for budget reallocation is nevertheless constrained by absorptive capacity. Under a threefold capacity cap and an assumption that costs rise with the square root of scale, the relatively efficient instruments can absorb an additional 11.0 percentage points of the budget, with the model indicating a net increase of 7.5 per cent in applications. A further 37.8 percentage points cannot be allocated to these instruments within the specified efficiency and capacity assumptions, indicating that additional capacity would be required before a larger reallocation could be accommodated without exhausting their estimated cost advantage.
items.title: ANALYSIS OF EXISTING MARKETING INSTRUMENTS FOR THE PROMOTION OF UNIVERSITY EDUCATIONAL SERVICES: STAGE REACH, THE COST-EFFICIENCY INVERSION, AND THE ABSORPTIVE CAPACITY CONSTRAINT

items.summary: Code, 2.5-D finite-wavelength forward solver, datasets, trained models and result files reproducing every number in the manuscript "Source-Conditioned Neural Surrogates for Magnetotelluric Response Prediction Under Finite-Wavelength Excitation" (S. Oh). The study makes the magnetotelluric source an explicit input of a neural forward surrogate. A validated 2.5-D scattered-field solver for a source of finite along-strike wavelength generates the training data; a conditional U-Net predicts the electromagnetic fields, from which impedance and tipper are reconstructed; an aliasing ratio quantifies how much of a source perturbation a plane-wave inversion re-images as conductivity; a surrogate-domain recoverability experiment returns a source estimate close to the known synthetic value, while a direct solver re-forward shows that the recovered conductivity and wavenumber are not together a solver-consistent inverse solution; and magnetometer arrays at three geomagnetic latitudes place real settings on the dimensionless axis that the model defines. CONTENTS: README.md, LICENSE, DATA_LICENSE.txt and requirements.txt are attached unpacked. The code archive holds the analysis scripts (top level and mt3d/) and the full solver source (solver/, with the dataset generator, the Jacobian dump, the re-forward program and the unit tests); it is MIT licensed except the third-party Triangle library, which is redistributed verbatim under its own terms. The data archive holds the three datasets (dataset_dense, dataset_freq, dataset40), the trained checkpoints (ckpt/, mt3d/ckpt/), the joint-inversion and layered-earth training data (mt3d/*.npz), the plane-wave Jacobian dump (phase3/), the solver sweeps (phase1_repro/) and the result files next to the scripts that write them, all under CC BY 4.0 (DATA_LICENSE.txt). Figures and figure-drawing scripts are not included; every figure is a direct plot of a listed result file. Comments have been removed from all code written for this study. Not included: the magnetometer-array time series, which are third-party open data (EarthScope/USArray MT through the IRIS/EarthScope Data Management Center; AusLAMP Musgraves/APY through AuScope and Geoscience Australia, CC BY 4.0) and are rebuilt from those sources by the archived fetch and conversion scripts; and the field-station file that supplies the period list of the two control tests of Section S-XVII (available from the author on request).
items.title: Source-Conditioned Residual Learning for Magnetotelluric Responses Under Finite-Wavelength Excitation

items.summary: We establish the overarching mathematical physics framework underlying gravitational screening and electroweak mixing in Big Boot Gauge Theory (BBGT). To demonstrate that the transition from the bare gravitational constant G_bare = 6.514085763e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 (derived from CODATA 2022 constants under unit space-time momentum p = mc = 1 kg m s^-1) to the observed value G_obs = 6.67430e-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 is a rigorous topological necessity rather than an arbitrary post-hoc adjustment, we formulate the screening dynamics using Möbius inversion on finite posets over the subgroup lattice of Poincaré Dodecahedral Space (S^3/I^*). We prove that non-associative transit across the e_4 Pati-Salam midpoint node acts as a Möbius topological twist, fixing the geometric inverse-square screening factor S_ZIP^-2 = (1 - 1/120)^-2 = 1.016877348. Combining this with longitudinal Z-leakage (delta_Z = 0.026892000) and non-associative midpoint transit corrections (Delta_assoc = 0.000092701) yields the exact screened laboratory constant without arbitrary tuning.  Furthermore, we demonstrate that the weak mixing angle (sin^2 theta_W = 1/5 + 1/32 = 0.23125) originates from the pentagonal P_5 symmetry order of the dodecahedron combined with a 2^5 chiral energy cascade, agreeing with experiment (0.23122) to within 0.01%. Finally, we present the complete 8x8 Logical Transitive Index Matrix (T_{n->m}), showing how the 10^19 Planck-to-electroweak mass hierarchy is compressed down to a discrete compilation factor of 128.35 across the aethereal boot levels.

items.title: Topological Invariance of Gravitational Screening in Big Boot Gauge Theory: Möbius Poset Inversion, Pentagonal Mixing, and the T_{n->m} Transitive Hierarchy

items.summary: Solutions to geophysical inverse problems are generally non-unique, and greatly benefit from additional geological prior information. Generative Neural Networks (GNNs) are commonly used to parametrise such information, typically restricting solutions to a lower-dimensional latent space. The final inversion result is obtained by mapping the latent space parameters to the original higher-dimensional model space using the GNNs. However, solutions then remain confined to a low-dimensional geological generative manifold; if the true Earth model lies outside of this manifold, standard latent space inversion fails. We propose a Bayesian model space inversion method that uses the generative manifold as a guide to find the solutions that lie outside this manifold. We validate our approach in non-linear travel-time tomography experiments on both simple and more geological structures. By comparing our method with model space inversion using uniform prior probabilities and standard latent-space inversion, we demonstrate that the less informative uniform prior fails to constrain the solution, while the latent space approach fails when the true Earth model lies outside of the generative manifold. Conversely, our new model-space inversion method successfully recovers complex off-manifold geological features while maintaining low solution uncertainty.
items.title: Escaping Geological Generative Prior Distributions in Bayesian Travel Time Tomography

items.summary: Methods that recover individual latent variables of the world, from nonlinear ICA to dictionary learning and causal representation learning, anchor the latents to observations through reconstruction, auxiliary supervision, or distributional asymmetries such as non-Gaussianity. Methods without these anchors, including joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs), identify the latent state only up to a linear transformation, so individual latents remain mixed. We close this gap: individual world latents can be provably recovered with no reconstruction, no decoder, and no labels. The key condition is Structural Diversity: different latents leave distinct dependency footprints on observations, just as no two snowflakes are alike. Building on the linear identifiability that LeJEPA provides, we prove that under Structural Diversity, DSReg (Dependency-Sparsity Regularization) recovers individual world latents up to signed permutation, without reconstruction or a decoder. It applies post hoc to any linearly identified representation, reusing trained checkpoints at no loss over joint training, and establishes the first fully identifiable JEPA that recovers every world latent. Moreover, as a condition on dependency footprints, Structural Diversity is strictly weaker than all structural conditions of prior identifiable latent variable models. Across synthetic regimes, world model probes, learned visual encoders, and external renderers, DSReg preserves dense prediction while improving individual-latent recovery and downstream use with scales.
items.title: DSReg: Provably Recovering Individual World Latents without Reconstruction

items.summary: Physics-based models connect scientific explanation with quantitative prediction. Constructing them requires selecting physical processes, defining states and governing equations, specifying couplings, and identifying parameters from experiments. Existing AI systems remain limited in making these model structure decisions autonomously. We introduce EvoSim, a self-evolving AI scientist for physical modeling. It uses experimental discrepancies to drive mechanism and equation revisions and held-out experimental data to test physical plausibility. Exploration traces make updates to knowledge, skills, and multi-agent orchestration. This co-evolution improves physics-based models and EvoSim's ability to select mechanisms, diagnose failures, and coordinate research. We evaluate EvoSim on two industrial battery modeling tasks. It predicts lithium-metal-plating onset from 25 to 45 degrees Celsius and 2 C to 6 C with a mean absolute error of 1.79% in state of charge. Dynamic voltage prediction under vehicle driving conditions achieves a root mean square error of 7.62 mV, surpassing the reported accuracy of models developed by human experts. Self-evolution reduces model and physics errors by approximately 36% relative to baseline, demonstrating improved scientific modeling capability. EvoSim turns experimental observations into validated models and cumulative research expertise.
items.title: EvoSim: Learning to Model, Modeling to Learn

items.summary: Offline MARL increasingly relies on generative policies to model multimodal joint behavior, typically by distilling a centralized teacher into decentralized one-step actors under the CTDE. We identify a failure mode at the teacher training stage: standard flow-based teachers pair noise with replay targets independently, so nearby noise samples can be routed toward conflicting coordination modes. The teacher then produces samples between valid modes, and because the distillation loss regresses each local actor onto the conditional mean of the teacher's output given local input, this error is not absorbed but propagated to the student. To remove this teacher-side artifact, we propose Mode-Support Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport (MoSDOT), which summarizes multimodal replay into a finite mode support with prescribed capacities and uses conditional semi-discrete optimal transport to assign each noise sample to a single mode before teacher training. We additionally study a shared-randomness variant that uses a shared noise component at execution to expose the residual gap intrinsic to strict-product execution. On controlled diagnostics and offline MARL benchmarks, MoSDOT improves endpoint quality and routing consistency, particularly on datasets exhibiting multimodal joint behavior.
items.title: Multi-Agent Coordination via Support-Preserving Distillation

items.summary: Self-contained computational materials accompanying "Verifiable approval-release decisions for construction project management: A provenance-aware contract and automated evidence" by Ahmad Baghdadi. Version 4.0.0 includes source code, complete generated inputs and results, schemas, exact witnesses, a de-identified calendar encoding, benchmark records and SHA-256 checksums. This version adds 83 conventional priority-list levelling comparisons under identical constraints: 72 tied peaks and 11 one-gate improvements, with sufficient exact certificates for all 83. A complete two-plan PROV-O example passes the domain and provenance SHACL profiles and preserves every decision field after RDF exchange. The suite comprises 145 automated tests. Earlier computational evidence includes generated extraction, 360 controlled record comparisons, exact wave bounds, nine calendar scenarios and 80 saved benchmark plans with renewed arithmetic audit. S14 preparation includes blank independent-annotation and approval registers plus a precision/recall evaluator with explicit denominators. No native baseline or independent annotations are available; field validation has not been executed. Case A remains historical aggregates only. Calendar B is a prior encoding with assumed review windows. Supplementary Table S1 identifies the deposited components and the supplement consolidates the evidence limits.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for verifiable approval-release decisions in construction project management

items.summary: Code, preregistration record and derived data for a manuscript submitted to Environmental Impact Assessment Review. audit.py reproduces every figure and number in the paper through twenty-one pipeline stages and writes a per-stage log with stdout hashes; the last stage checks that every number printed in the manuscript and its tables is traceable to a file the pipeline writes, and exits non-zero if one is not. The deposit contains the analysis scripts, the preregistration record with its revision history, the derived per-point attributes for the 799 labelled points — lithological class and fault distance — the literature weight extraction, the figures, the audit log, and the anonymized manuscript and supplementary material that the last stage reads. The primary sources are not redistributed: the geological mapping and fault traces of the Hellenic Survey of Geology and Mineral Exploration are available under institutional access only. See README.md for each source and its access terms; MANIFEST.txt lists every deposited file with its md5. Changes since v1.1: the target journal is Environmental Impact Assessment Review rather than Omega; a twenty-first stage checks the provenance of every number in the submitted documents; the comparison of the two lithological codings is a stage rather than two runs sequenced by hand, after a clean pass was found to leave both codings’ outputs holding the same distribution; the Fisher’s exact test of the permeability contrast, previously computed outside the pipeline, is computed by the script that draws Figure S2; the figure scripts share figstyle.py, which embeds TrueType fonts and pins the font family, after two runs of the same pipeline produced figures in two different typefaces; fig2.py and fig3.py, which produce two of the submitted figures, were added to the audit, having been outside it; range_weights.py replaces a script that had been deleted; rapidfuzz is declared in requirements.txt after a silent fallback had changed the scheme count from 129 to 125; and make_deposit.py builds the archive from an explicit list instead of by hand.
items.title: Code and derived data for: Can decision records validate criterion weights? Resampling evidence from 73 documented siting decisions

items.summary: Version 1.1.0 makes a typed RASS evidence extension the representation backbone beneath the action-specific evidence contract. Its full-domain quantitative core follows the real amply soft-set (RASS) representation, while categorical payload, evidence status, provenance and acquisition metadata remain separate companions. Native records are projected onto a 29-coordinate universe with nested T0--T3 active sets; scalars, genuine intervals, categorical values and explicit empty-state reasons retain their native semantics. Audits confirm 192/192 enumerated routing-state matches, exact projection of 80/80 frozen held-out feature entries and 80/80 required-coordinate inactivity checks. A content-addressed contract manifest records the representation, support, action, loss, risk denominators and frozen artifact hashes; an outcome-blind refinement audit verifies nested qualification sets at 300, 360 and 500 cycles and binds all 60 frozen horizon-specific decisions to unique traces. The evidence contract supplies authorization semantics, while the frozen predictor, calibration, held-out decisions and empirical results remain unchanged. The package includes the immutable pre-open snapshot, derived development and external-admissibility audits, unit tests, figures and file-level SHA-256 manifests. Raw provider datasets and private overlap ledgers are not redistributed.
items.title: Evidence-contract knowledge system for auditable second-life battery qualification: reproducibility package

items.summary: Analysis code and computed evidence store for the manuscript "An exact recurrence test for acquisition-chain bounds in vehicle telemetry: the closed ECU surface yields nothing, and the one detection lies in the logger we built ourselves", submitted to Sensors and Actuators A: Physical. This deposit contains code and derived results only. The underlying telemetry is published separately under its own DOIs, which fetch_data.py downloads and checksum-verifies before analysis, so the published figures are reproducible from the public record. Study design: observational audit of already-deposited telemetry (seven recording sessions). No experimental control, no intervention, no independent replication, and no statistical power for population-level inference. Headlines formulated after measurement rather than pre-declared in config.json are labelled exploratory in the manuscript. Multiplicity: this deposit is one of 15 analyses drawn from the same corpus of seven sessions, one vehicle and one rider. No correction for multiple comparisons is applied across that family, so the family-wise error rate is not controlled. Repository commit of record: 37f7b2147b26
items.title: Reproducibility package (I-21): An exact recurrence test for acquisition-chain bounds in vehicle telemetry: the closed ECU surface yields nothing, and the one detection lies in the logger we built ourselves

items.summary: Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Microsoft Planetary Computer (MPC) both distribute Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance, and their outputs can be combined in a single time series. Over one 73 ha cattle farm in northern Colombia, we tested whether the two platforms yield the same parcel-scale vegetation and water indices and, where they differ, at which layer the difference originates: the product, the processing chain or the scene universe. For identical products, scene classification and harmonised reflectance matched in every comparable pixel, and the same chain executed locally or server-side in GEE gave per-scene indices and monthly medians that agreed within 1e-6. The catalogues, however, did not hold the same scenes: between June 2024 and April 2025, 10 of 146 scene–tile records existed only in GEE, six of them Sentinel-2C records, and none only in MPC; in 22 of 136 common records, all from June–July 2024, the catalogues held different L2A generations of the same acquisition. In the two monthly composites tested over the farm, the GEE-only scenes shifted mean NDVI by −0.0005 and −0.0087; over a public 1 km² demonstration area with the same scene inventory, the shift reached −0.028 (January 2025). Files: - Pantevez-Villamil_2026_GEE-MPC-Sentinel2_preprint_v1.pdf — preprint (English), not peer reviewed. - Pantevez-Villamil_2026_GEE-MPC-Sentinel2_data_v1.zip — reconciliation table with scene identifiers, processing baselines and cloud cover; E2 analysis; scene lists and SHA-256 hashes of each composite; monthly metrics and per-pixel difference distributions; evidence tables for Section 3.2; public demonstration area of interest and tool outputs on it. The farm geometry is not included (landowner privacy). - Pantevez-Villamil_2026_GEE-MPC-Sentinel2_code_v1.0.0.zip — three Python tools (MIT licence), Spanish-language guide, acceptance test and workflow figures. Code in the software archive is released under the MIT licence. Catalogues queried on 24 September 2026. Developed within the Curso de Percepción Remota Avanzada, Doctorado en Agroecología, Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Sede Bogotá. Generative AI assistants (Claude, Anthropic; ChatGPT, OpenAI) supported test design, code, literature search, review and drafting; the author verified all results and is responsible for the content.
items.title: Same computation, different scenes: a single-site comparison of Sentinel-2 L2A composites from Google Earth Engine and Microsoft Planetary Computer

items.summary: This record provides the public, non-confidential analytical and reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “When Does Seismic–Geotechnical Data Fusion Add Value? A Borehole-Aware Empirical-to-Synthetic Validation Framework for Urban Tunnelling.” The study develops and audits a borehole-aware empirical-to-synthetic framework for evaluating whether adding downhole seismic information provides defensible incremental value in predicting the Ménard pressuremeter modulus under held-out validation. The empirical benchmark comprises 41 support-matched pressuremeter–seismic records across 21 independent boreholes from the Isfahan Metro Line 2 investigation. The framework compares a reference model, a geotechnical/geological-depth baseline, a seismic-only branch, naive multimodal fusion, and a dependence-aware fusion branch using leave-one-borehole-out validation. items.summary: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MASs) are increasingly used to solve complex tasks through coordinated reasoning, tool use, and interaction with external resources. However, attributing failures in such systems remains challenging because the observed outcome often does not directly reveal the error responsible for the failed execution. In this work, the attribution target is the decisive error, defined as the agent--step pair whose correction would recover the failed execution. Existing approaches largely identify suspicious steps without explicitly modeling how errors propagate across interactions or persist in unresolved loops, making decisive errors difficult to distinguish from downstream failure symptoms. We propose \textbf{E}rror-Propagation \textbf{M}odeling for \textbf{F}ailure \textbf{A}ttribution (\textbf{EMFA}). EMFA constructs a structured representation of the failed trajectory, models both cascading propagation and persistent interaction loops, and uses propagation-aware candidate screening followed by counterfactual verification to identify the decisive agent--step pair. On the Who\&When benchmark, EMFA achieves state-of-the-art step-level attribution accuracy and remains competitive at the agent level. It improves the previous best step-level results by 3.45 and 4.40 percentage points on the Hand-Crafted and Algorithm-Generated subsets, respectively.
items.title: Error-Propagation Modeling for Failure Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a comment on a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview and comments at https://prereview.org/reviews/22745390 . Thank you, Evgenii, for the detailed and constructive PREreview. Your comments led us to substantially strengthen both the experimental design and the interpretation of the results. We have now released a revised version of the manuscript that addresses the main points raised in the review. The revision includes: A 30-seed robustness analysis rather than relying on a single simulation seed A correlation sweep for estimator errors from ρ = 0 to 0.8 Regression-fitted and test-set oracle aggregation baselines Shared-noise experiments for the model–collective calibration signal, reported with ROC-AUC and lift Explicit specification of the four-Wave rolling calibration window, software versions, and PCG64 RNG Portfolio scaling to 100 Feature Blocks using an exact binary MILP reference An explicit separation between budget-constrained portfolio selection and ODP's native dependency-aware sequencing role An exact and scaling benchmark for ODP sequencing under prerequisite constraints An explicit competing-interest disclosure A public reproducibility package containing the simulation code, deterministic seeds, generated data, analysis scripts, and validation material. One particularly useful outcome of the revision was that the stronger experiments narrowed some of our original claims. For example, inverse-MSE aggregation performs very strongly when estimator errors are independent, but its advantage collapses under strong shared error. We also found that ODP distance is not the strongest heuristic for budget-constrained portfolio selection, while it performs very differently in its native sequencing role, where ERS/BVS is exactly optimal for the declared objective without dependencies and remains close to the exact optimum under the tested prerequisite constraints. Revised manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10648 Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23261325 Thank you again for the review. It improved the paper. Competing interests I am a co-author of the manuscript discussed in this PREreview and a contributor to the D-POAF framework evaluated in the study. I am also affiliated with Inovionix, which develops software implementing D-POAF concepts.

items.summary: Offline MARL increasingly relies on generative policies to model multimodal joint behavior, typically by distilling a centralized teacher into decentralized one-step actors under the CTDE. We identify a failure mode at the teacher training stage: standard flow-based teachers pair noise with replay targets independently, so nearby noise samples can be routed toward conflicting coordination modes. The teacher then produces samples between valid modes, and because the distillation loss regresses each local actor onto the conditional mean of the teacher's output given local input, this error is not absorbed but propagated to the student. To remove this teacher-side artifact, we propose Mode-Support Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport (MoSDOT), which summarizes multimodal replay into a finite mode support with prescribed capacities and uses conditional semi-discrete optimal transport to assign each noise sample to a single mode before teacher training. We additionally study a shared-randomness variant that uses a shared noise component at execution to expose the residual gap intrinsic to strict-product execution. On controlled diagnostics and offline MARL benchmarks, MoSDOT improves endpoint quality and routing consistency, particularly on datasets exhibiting multimodal joint behavior.
items.title: Multi-Agent Coordination via Support-Preserving Distillation

items.summary: Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Microsoft Planetary Computer (MPC) both distribute Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance, and their outputs can be combined in a single time series. Over one 73 ha cattle farm in northern Colombia, we tested whether the two platforms yield the same parcel-scale vegetation and water indices and, where they differ, at which layer the difference originates: the product, the processing chain or the scene universe. For identical products, scene classification and harmonised reflectance matched in every comparable pixel, and the same chain executed locally or server-side in GEE gave per-scene indices and monthly medians that agreed within 1e-6. The catalogues, however, did not hold the same scenes: between June 2024 and April 2025, 10 of 146 scene–tile records existed only in GEE, six of them Sentinel-2C records, and none only in MPC; in 22 of 136 common records, all from June–July 2024, the catalogues held different L2A generations of the same acquisition. In the two monthly composites tested over the farm, the GEE-only scenes shifted mean NDVI by −0.0005 and −0.0087; over a public 1 km² demonstration area with the same scene inventory, the shift reached −0.028 (January 2025). Files: - Pantevez-Villamil_2026_GEE-MPC-Sentinel2_preprint_v1.pdf — preprint (English), not peer reviewed. - Pantevez-Villamil_2026_GEE-MPC-Sentinel2_data_v1.zip — reconciliation table with scene identifiers, processing baselines and cloud cover; E2 analysis; scene lists and SHA-256 hashes of each composite; monthly metrics and per-pixel difference distributions; evidence tables for Section 3.2; public demonstration area of interest and tool outputs on it. The farm geometry is not included (landowner privacy). - Pantevez-Villamil_2026_GEE-MPC-Sentinel2_code_v1.0.0.zip — three Python tools (MIT licence), Spanish-language guide, acceptance test and workflow figures. Code in the software archive is released under the MIT licence. Catalogues queried on 24 September 2026. Developed within the Curso de Percepción Remota Avanzada, Doctorado en Agroecología, Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias, Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Sede Bogotá. Generative AI assistants (Claude, Anthropic; ChatGPT, OpenAI) supported test design, code, literature search, review and drafting; the author verified all results and is responsible for the content.
items.title: Same computation, different scenes: a single-site comparison of Sentinel-2 L2A composites from Google Earth Engine and Microsoft Planetary Computer

items.summary: The present study was undertaken to establish pharmacognostic standards and phytochemical profiles of two ethnomedicinally important plants, Cajanus goensis and Sarcostigma kleinii. Both species are traditionally employed in the treatment of rheumatism, inflammatory disorders, and other systemic ailments, yet scientific validation of their crude drug parameters remains limited. Standardization of herbal materials is essential to ensure identity, purity, and reproducibility, thereby reducing variability and enhancing therapeutic reliability. In this study, plant materials were procured from authentic local sources—Cajanus goensis from Udaipur, Rajasthan, and Sarcostigma kleinii from Latur, Maharashtra—and subjected to comprehensive pharmacognostic and phytochemical evaluation. Organoleptic analysis revealed distinct sensory characteristics, with Cajanus goensis exhibiting greenish-brown coloration, earthy odor, and coarse texture, while Sarcostigma kleinii showed yellowish-brown coloration, pungent odor, and oily texture. Macroscopic and microscopic examinations confirmed diagnostic features such as dorsiventral leaves, reticulate venation, thick cuticular layers, and prominent vascular bundles. Physico-chemical evaluation demonstrated that ash values, extractive values, moisture content, and pH were within pharmacopoeial limits, thereby confirming the purity and stability of the crude drugs. Notably, Cajanus goensis exhibited higher alcohol-soluble extractives, while Sarcostigma kleinii showed greater water-soluble extractives, reflecting differences in phytoconstituent solubility. Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of carbohydrates, amino acids, alkaloids, glycosides, flavonoids, tannins, and phenolic compounds in both species. Proteins were detected only in Sarcostigma kleinii, while saponins were present exclusively in Cajanus goensis. Sterols were absent in both plants, highlighting unique chemical signatures that aid in authentication. Quantitative estimation confirmed that both species are rich in flavonoids and phenolic compounds, with Sarcostigma kleinii showing slightly higher concentrations (21.06 ± 1.000 mg/g quercetin equivalents and 21.19 ± 0.854 mg/g tannic acid equivalents) compared to Cajanus goensis (19.09 ± 0.444 mg/g and 18.49 ± 0.033 mg/g, respectively). These bioactive constituents are well recognized for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, supporting the traditional use of these plants in rheumatism and related disorders. In conclusion, the study provides reproducible pharmacognostic and phytochemical data for Cajanus goensis and Sarcostigma kleinii, thereby validating their ethnomedicinal claims and establishing a foundation for further pharmacological investigations. The results underscore the importance of standardization in herbal medicine and highlight the potential of these crude drugs as reliable sources of bioactive compounds for future therapeutic applications.
tags: Cajanus goensis; Sarcostigma kleinii; crude drug standardization; phytochemical screening; flavonoids; phenolic compounds; rheumatism; pharmacognosy; herbal medicine; quality control.
items.title: Standardization And Phytochemical Profiling of Cajanus Goensis and Sarcostigma Kleinii: Establishing Baseline Parameters for Crude Drug Evaluation

items.summary: This repository contains the curated research inputs, analysis code, and reference outputs supporting the study “Supplier identity can reverse estimates of global irrigation savings.” The study examines whether estimates of global irrigation savings depend on which suppliers reduce production, even when displacement quantities are held fixed within each market. It combines crop production, trade, and water-use data with constrained allocation models, historical production-contraction benchmarks, alternative water accounts, and conditional future scenarios for 2050 and 2100. Repository contents 01_Research_Inputs.xlsx — Curated source observations, geographic and crop identifiers, variable definitions, and source citations. 02_Research_Data.sqlite — Larger input datasets, archived analytical outputs, numerical checks, optional derived checkpoints, and an index linking the release to the associated manuscript and supplementary material. Source inputs and computed outputs are explicitly distinguished. 03_Analysis.py — Consolidated Python code containing the analytical modules, dependency specifications, input verification, and reproduction workflow. 04_Readme.txt — Documentation of data provenance, units, assumptions, reproduction instructions, licensing, and file checksums. The release corresponds to six main-text figures, 16 supplementary figures, and 24 supplementary tables. The exact associated manuscript and supplementary document versions are identified by their SHA-256 fingerprints. Data sources include ACEA, FAOSTAT, CWASI, GCAM scenario outputs, USGS irrigation water-use estimates, Kansas irrigation-technology replication data, and complementary water-account datasets. Source-specific citations and attribution requirements are retained in the documentation. Reproduction and validation The documented workflow uses Python 3.11. Separate dependency environments are specified where required. Installing dependencies requires internet access; the numerical analyses use the deposited inputs. Instructions cover the complete workflow and targeted reproduction checks. For version 1.0.1, file checksums, database integrity, and embedded assets were verified. The full-routing analysis was rerun from the deposited GCAM inputs for all 50 future configurations, reproducing the archived global water bounds and joint conservation outcomes within numerical tolerance. This targeted validation does not constitute a new execution of every stage of the study. Interpretation and reuse The modeled water bounds are conditional on specified technology responses, market quantities, supplier availability, production constraints, and water-use coefficients. They are not confidence intervals or globally identified causal effects of irrigation-technology adoption. Future configurations are conditional stress tests, not probabilistic forecasts. Original data compilations and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0, and original analysis code under the MIT License. Third-party inputs retain their source-specific licenses and attribution requirements, as documented in the README. Please cite this repository and the relevant original data sources when reusing the materials.
items.title: Data and code for "Supplier identity can reverse estimates of global irrigation savings"

items.summary: The emerging low-altitude economy demands unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for reliable connectivity and environmental awareness. In particular, embodied UAV agents offer a promising means of supporting autonomous operations through a closed loop linking perception, decision-making, and physical actions. However, each UAV has access only to local observations, and effective cooperation requires exchanging local states and intentions. Directly sharing such information can incur substantial signaling overhead and hinder timely coordination in dynamic environments. To deal with this problem, this paper investigates a cooperative ISAC network of embodied UAV agents and formulates a joint token communications (TokCom) and physical control problem to minimize total propulsion energy subject to communication and sensing rate requirements. Then, we propose a state--intent TokCom (SI-TokCom) framework driven by multi-agent embodied policy learning. Specifically, separate pretrained codebooks enable compact exchanges of local states and intentions, while UAV agents jointly learn to select and compose tokens and determine physical actions based on local observations and received tokens. Simulation results show that SI-TokCom achieves 98.9\% and 99.1\% of the centralized baseline's communication and sensing rates, respectively. Compared with the local baseline, it improves the corresponding rates by 5.0\% and 43.6\%, respectively, with essentially unchanged propulsion energy. These results highlight the potential of TokCom for communication-efficient cooperation among embodied UAV agents in ISAC systems.
items.title: An Embodied Multiagent Framework Based on Token Communications for Cooperative ISAC

items.summary: Token-based world models enable fine-grained latent planning, but repeatedly processing large spatial token grids makes action search expensive. We introduce COSTGRAD, a training-free, goal-conditioned selector that ranks spatial tokens by the gradient norm of the planning cost with respect to each input token. By deriving importance from the downstream control objective, COSTGRAD targets tokens that matter for planning rather than merely for prediction. On AdaLN-conditioned predictors at $50\%$ sparsity, COSTGRAD matches or exceeds full-token planning on three of four continuous-control benchmarks, while giving a measured $2.6\times$ wall-clock speedup per environment planning step. Combining token sparsity with reduced CEM search increases this to a $\sim 5\times$ total speedup while still exceeding the full-token baseline. We also identify an architecture-dependent failure mode: in a matched AdaLN-vs-concat comparison, concat maintains comparable full-token performance but pure COSTGRAD loses its advantage over random selection. This difference tracks action-pathway drift: gradient-selected removal produces less drift than random removal on AdaLN, but more on concat. These results highlight selector-architecture compatibility as a design axis for sparse world-model planning. Project page and demos: https://ycxuyingchen.github.io/costgrad/
items.title: Sparse Planning in Visual World Models via Cost Gradients

items.summary: Robot foundation models provide strong visuomotor control, yet their performance can degrade when object positions or task instructions change. Further improvements often require post-training on substantial robot data, which can be costly to collect through methods such as teleoperation. Agentic harnesses can adapt around the model, but current self-evolving harnesses use robot trials inefficiently when deciding which code and skill changes to pursue. We introduce EmbodiedRSI, a self-evolving agentic harness that autonomously decides where to explore next and turns the resulting physical interaction into improved code and skills. EmbodiedRSI realizes this through a Fast-Slow Dual-System Architecture, in which competing code and skill hypotheses are maintained in a Hypothesis Graph. Value-of-Information Experiment Selection chooses physical experiments that can distinguish these hypotheses. Their outcomes guide Code-Skill Co-Evolution. The Slow System builds Hierarchical Memory, and Reward-Grounded Memory Learning selects effective memory according to their value for later Fast-System improvement. On RoboCasa365, EmbodiedRSI reaches 77.0% overall success and 71.3% on Composite-Unseen, compared with 40.1% for the best baseline. EmbodiedRSI also reaches 86.8% overall success on LIBERO-Pro. Beyond benchmark performance, EmbodiedRSI transfers zero-shot to real-world robot, achieving 71.3% overall success across multiple challenging tasks.
items.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution

items.summary: Physics-based models connect scientific explanation with quantitative prediction. Constructing them requires selecting physical processes, defining states and governing equations, specifying couplings, and identifying parameters from experiments. Existing AI systems remain limited in making these model structure decisions autonomously. We introduce EvoSim, a self-evolving AI scientist for physical modeling. It uses experimental discrepancies to drive mechanism and equation revisions and held-out experimental data to test physical plausibility. Exploration traces make updates to knowledge, skills, and multi-agent orchestration. This co-evolution improves physics-based models and EvoSim's ability to select mechanisms, diagnose failures, and coordinate research. We evaluate EvoSim on two industrial battery modeling tasks. It predicts lithium-metal-plating onset from 25 to 45 degrees Celsius and 2 C to 6 C with a mean absolute error of 1.79% in state of charge. Dynamic voltage prediction under vehicle driving conditions achieves a root mean square error of 7.62 mV, surpassing the reported accuracy of models developed by human experts. Self-evolution reduces model and physics errors by approximately 36% relative to baseline, demonstrating improved scientific modeling capability. EvoSim turns experimental observations into validated models and cumulative research expertise.
items.title: EvoSim: Learning to Model, Modeling to Learn

items.summary: Version 1.1.0 makes a typed RASS evidence extension the representation backbone beneath the action-specific evidence contract. Its full-domain quantitative core follows the real amply soft-set (RASS) representation, while categorical payload, evidence status, provenance and acquisition metadata remain separate companions. Native records are projected onto a 29-coordinate universe with nested T0--T3 active sets; scalars, genuine intervals, categorical values and explicit empty-state reasons retain their native semantics. Audits confirm 192/192 enumerated routing-state matches, exact projection of 80/80 frozen held-out feature entries and 80/80 required-coordinate inactivity checks. A content-addressed contract manifest records the representation, support, action, loss, risk denominators and frozen artifact hashes; an outcome-blind refinement audit verifies nested qualification sets at 300, 360 and 500 cycles and binds all 60 frozen horizon-specific decisions to unique traces. The evidence contract supplies authorization semantics, while the frozen predictor, calibration, held-out decisions and empirical results remain unchanged. The package includes the immutable pre-open snapshot, derived development and external-admissibility audits, unit tests, figures and file-level SHA-256 manifests. Raw provider datasets and private overlap ledgers are not redistributed.
items.title: Evidence-contract knowledge system for auditable second-life battery qualification: reproducibility package

items.summary: v1.0.0 — Initial Audited Analysis Code Release Initial public release of the audited analysis code supporting: Cross-Cohort Transportability, Calibration, and Incremental Value of Breast DCE-MRI Radiomics for Predicting Pathologic Complete Response Included Preprocessing and cohort preparation scripts DCE-MRI radiomics extraction workflow Clinical, radiomics, and combined modeling pipelines Internal and external validation scripts Bootstrap comparison analyses Figure-generation scripts Reproducibility and analysis-workflow documentation Version-pinned Python environment Reproducibility scope This release contains the audited analysis code and documentation used for the reported analyses. No patient-level data, medical images, masks, prediction files, or derived radiomics matrices are distributed in this repository. Three historical provenance gaps are explicitly documented in the repository and should be considered when interpreting end-to-end reproducibility. Data The analyses use publicly available breast DCE-MRI resources. Dataset access information and applicable licensing are documented in docs/DATA_AVAILABILITY.md . License Code in this repository is released under the MIT License. Dataset licenses remain governed by their respective data providers. Release: v1.0.0 Release date: 2026-10-08
items.title: Cross-Cohort Transportability, Calibration, and Incremental Value of Breast DCE-MRI Radiomics for Predicting Pathologic Complete Response

items.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) dispatch is beginning to move beyond isolated path planning and optimization-driven resource allocation toward system-level coordination supported by semantic reasoning and LLM-based interfaces. This survey provides a unified characterization of LLM-enabled UAV dispatch systems that bridges semantic intent, symbolic decision-making, and physical UAV execution. Rather than treating LLMs as standalone add-ons, we conceptualize them as a cross-layer semantic orchestration layer connecting human instructions, external solvers, and distributed control modules. We organize the literature into four representative dispatch paradigms: pipeline dispatch, global assignment dispatch, decentralized agentic dispatch, and divide-and-conquer dispatch. For each paradigm, we analyze its decision logic, system structure, control flow, representative methods, and potential LLM roles. We further examine how LLMs support semantic parsing, retrieval-grounded planning, solver orchestration, local agent reasoning, multi-agent coordination, safety assessment, and human-facing explanation. We discuss the implications of these paradigms for scalability, robustness, coordination burden, and verification requirements, and identify open challenges including latency-aware reasoning, grounding reliability, physical feasibility guarantees, edge deployment, privacy protection, and distributed consistency. This survey provides a system-level taxonomy and design perspective for integrating LLMs into safety-critical UAV dispatch systems.
items.title: LLM-Enabled UAV Dispatch: A System-Level Survey and Taxonomy

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a comment on a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview and comments at https://prereview.org/reviews/22745390 . Thank you, Evgenii, for the detailed and constructive PREreview. Your comments led us to substantially strengthen both the experimental design and the interpretation of the results. We have now released a revised version of the manuscript that addresses the main points raised in the review. The revision includes: A 30-seed robustness analysis rather than relying on a single simulation seed A correlation sweep for estimator errors from ρ = 0 to 0.8 Regression-fitted and test-set oracle aggregation baselines Shared-noise experiments for the model–collective calibration signal, reported with ROC-AUC and lift Explicit specification of the four-Wave rolling calibration window, software versions, and PCG64 RNG Portfolio scaling to 100 Feature Blocks using an exact binary MILP reference An explicit separation between budget-constrained portfolio selection and ODP's native dependency-aware sequencing role An exact and scaling benchmark for ODP sequencing under prerequisite constraints An explicit competing-interest disclosure A public reproducibility package containing the simulation code, deterministic seeds, generated data, analysis scripts, and validation material. One particularly useful outcome of the revision was that the stronger experiments narrowed some of our original claims. For example, inverse-MSE aggregation performs very strongly when estimator errors are independent, but its advantage collapses under strong shared error. We also found that ODP distance is not the strongest heuristic for budget-constrained portfolio selection, while it performs very differently in its native sequencing role, where ERS/BVS is exactly optimal for the declared objective without dependencies and remains close to the exact optimum under the tested prerequisite constraints. Revised manuscript: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10648 Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23261325 Thank you again for the review. It improved the paper. Competing interests I am a co-author of the manuscript discussed in this PREreview and a contributor to the D-POAF framework evaluated in the study. I am also affiliated with Inovionix, which develops software implementing D-POAF concepts.
items.title: Comment on a PREreview of "Governed Human-AI Prioritization Under Uncertainty: Adaptive Estimation and Dependency-Constrained Portfolio Selection"

items.summary: General-purpose agents increasingly write code, use tools, and complete complex digital tasks, raising the question of how far these capabilities carry into the physical world. To investigate this, we introduce RobotWorld, a challenging simulation testbed for robot use: turning instructions and observations into physical task execution through robot interfaces. Its 84 tasks span manipulation, mobile manipulation, locomotion, driving, and aerial control, with explicit interaction budgets and executable success checks. By analysing task outcomes alongside execution traces, we identify both the capabilities that transfer and the gaps that prevent reliable completion. Furthermore, we find that current agents can construct sophisticated perception and control workflows, including image segmentation, camera calibration, spatial estimation, and dynamics-based computation. These capabilities, however, do not consistently compose into successful behaviour: agents lose task-relevant object states despite reaching commanded poses, fail to correct ineffective actions, recover too late, or mistake unfinished tasks for completion. This uneven transfer also differs across models: Astra succeeds more often on spatial and constrained-contact goals, whereas Opus 5.5 succeeds more often on continuous-balance and timed-interaction goals. By linking these outcomes to execution behaviour, RobotWorld provides both a rigorous proving ground and an empirical account of the remaining capability gaps, thereby establishing concrete targets for training and designing more reliable physical-world agents.
items.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments

items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping how information is produced, accessed, and circulated, while enabling disinformation campaigns of increasing scale and sophistication. There is currently no clear evidence that fully autonomous AI swarms conduct influence operations at scale, but their enabling capabilities are advancing. We define malicious AI swarms as coordinated, persistent, and adaptive multi-agent systems designed for influence operations, distinguishing them from AI-assisted content production and centrally managed synthetic personas. We examine their implications for hybrid regimes and conflict-affected states in Africa, where institutional constraints and fragile media environments may heighten vulnerability. Drawing on Mali and Ethiopia, we consider how automated influence could infiltrate communities, fabricate consensus, and erode trust in governance and development. The cases illustrate different configurations of state and non-state influence: competing actors in Mali's fragmented information environment, and more organized state-led strategies of narrative management in Ethiopia. African-language and training-data asymmetries may constrain influence capabilities while weakening defensive responses. Hybrid human-AI operations could combine automated scale and adaptation with local knowledge and credibility. This forward-looking risk analysis develops a scenario of increasingly accessible AI-driven coordination, rather than claiming that autonomous swarms are already operating at scale in Africa. We propose a layered governance approach linking technical safeguards to platform accountability, civic institutions, and regional coordination to protect democratic participation, peacebuilding, and development.
items.title: Automated Disinformation and Malicious AI Swarms: Risks for Democracy and Development in Africa

items.summary: Replication package for a validation study of three off-the-shelf sentiment instruments (SenticNet 9, VADER, Twitter-RoBERTa) against blind three-coder human annotation on a stratified audit sample of 504 tweets, drawn from a collection of English-language tweets directed at six European airlines in the summers of 2018-2022 (252,650 user tweets after removal of re-captured records). The package contains, with no tweet text: tweet-level labels of all three instruments for every collected record (re-captured records and truncated author identifiers flagged); the 504 audited items with all three coders' original ratings, the original majority consensus, the post-audit adjudications and completed ratings, and a text-free linkage summary of each audited item's capture multiplicity; the codebook; the VADER and Twitter-RoBERTa scorers with the model revision; a conda environment manifest; and a single script (code/reproduce_all.py) that regenerates every statistic in the manuscript's tables, including the multiplicity-adjusted stratified difference estimates. See README.md for the layout, the sampling note, and the reproducibility boundaries (the historical SenticNet API run cannot be re-executed; the corpus cannot be rehydrated because platform identifiers were truncated at collection).
items.title: Replication package: Sentiment Instruments Are Not Interchangeable — Audited Validity, Its Descriptive Consequences, and Its Correction in Airline-Directed Twitter Discourse
